sources.publisher: Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado and Zhu
sources.review_note: Repeated strategy selection can overfit investment backtests.
Context-specific evaluation, independent review and ongoing monitoring.
Mint and freeze authority roles must be inspected separately.
Extensions can change token-transfer amounts and permissions.
Contract and administrative risks require independent assessment.
Bridging introduces separate settlement and trust dependencies.
External data sources introduce availability and integrity dependencies.
Margin and marking conventions depend on the derivative and clearing context.

lessons.title: Identity, units and venue boundaries
lessons.study_notes: A ticker is a display label. Identify the chain, network, venue and asset identifiers before interpreting a quote. Carry decimal precision and quote/base units through every calculation.
objectives: Distinguish token symbol from asset identity
Normalize exact units without floating-point rounding
Separate network availability from instrument eligibility

lessons.title: Reading markets and orders
lessons.study_notes: Read bid, ask, spread, depth, time and units together. A last-traded price is not an executable quote. Candles aggregate events and can conceal intrabar paths. A touched limit does not prove a fill; partial fills and order status require reconciliation.
objectives: Read OHLCV without assuming intrabar order
Distinguish market, limit, stop and stop-limit behavior
Track partial fills and remaining quantity

lessons.title: Fees, depth, slippage and impact
lessons.study_notes: Charge all known entry and exit costs. Pool impact arises from trade size and liquidity; slippage compares expected and received execution. Include spread, venue fees and chain costs. Missing cost conversion or insufficient depth is a reason to abstain.
objectives: Separate impact from slippage
Calculate net rather than gross outcomes
Refuse unknown fees or unsafe minimum output

lessons.title: Point-in-time data and missingness
lessons.study_notes: Features must have been available before the decision. Preserve source, event time, receipt time and availability time. A candle close or revised statistic cannot be used earlier than publication. Missing, stale and future values are not interchangeable with zero.
objectives: Detect future leakage and delayed publication
Treat stale or missing observations explicitly
Preserve source lineage and dataset splits

lessons.title: Capital, exposure and loss controls
lessons.study_notes: Keep available cash, committed cash, open exposure and correlated exposures separate. Apply configured order, position, loss and drawdown limits before admitting paper orders. Stops do not guarantee an exit price through a gap. Leverage, liquidation and funding require instrument-specific models.
objectives: Respect budgets including costs
Explain drawdown and loss limits
Recognize gap and leverage risk

lessons.title: Order lifecycle and outage drills
lessons.study_notes: An accepted request is not a settled fill. Preserve one intent identifier, reconcile uncertain status and prohibit blind retries. Halt on stale feeds, lost connectivity, mismatched networks or unclear settlement. Forum messages and unanimous model votes cannot authorize an order.
objectives: Reconcile uncertain orders without duplicates
Separate submitted, filled and settled states
Use kill switches and abstention

lessons.title: Scientific strategy evaluation
lessons.study_notes: Separate study, model fitting, validation, untouched evaluation and forward paper observation. Record every tested configuration and benchmark, include costs and test different regimes. A public practice answer key or a favorable backtest does not establish a tradable edge.
objectives: Avoid selection bias and repeated holdout tuning
Use chronological splits with horizon-aware gaps
Evaluate calibration, uncertainty and baselines

lessons.title: Portfolio behavior and changing regimes
lessons.study_notes: Evaluate aggregated risk across assets, networks and venues. Similar model pipelines can repeat the same error. Volatility, liquidity, correlation, depegs, liquidity withdrawals and macro events can change the decision domain. Historical correlations are uncertain rather than permanent rules.
objectives: Separate agreement from independent evidence
Detect distribution shift
Aggregate portfolio exposure

lessons.title: Key custody, approvals and untrusted information
lessons.study_notes: Read-only data and education credentials must not contain wallet signing authority. Treat retrieved content and agent conversations as untrusted. Inspect permissions and destinations independently. Login proof is distinct from transaction authorization; never provide seed phrases to a course or agent.
objectives: Protect secrets and limit privileges
Ignore instruction injection in external content
Check approvals and transaction meaning

lessons.title: Solana accounts, instructions and settlement
lessons.study_notes: Learn mint/program identity, token account ownership, decimal precision, SOL fees, instruction inspection, atomic rollback and commitment. Track validity and expiry from current network data, simulate where supported, and reconcile by the existing transaction identity before retrying.
objectives: Inspect signers, programs and token accounts
Handle failed transactions and expired blockhashes
Distinguish processed observations from stronger confirmation

lessons.title: Ethereum accounts, gas and approvals
lessons.study_notes: Learn chain-bound accounts, nonce ordering, gas budgets, receipts, approvals, contract calls and finality. Inclusion and successful execution differ. Replacing a pending transaction must preserve intended nonce semantics; bridge settlement adds separate dependencies and risks.
objectives: Read receipt status and gas consequences
Validate network identity and approvals
Handle nonce replacement and finality

lessons.title: BNB Smart Chain network-specific execution
lessons.study_notes: BNB Smart Chain has its own state, validators, fee environment and finality API. EVM compatibility does not make an Ethereum address balance, contract deployment or receipt interchangeable with BSC. Check the intended chain and current finalized state through the correct provider.
objectives: Separate BSC state from Ethereum state
Read chain-specific finality
Identify native gas requirements independently

lessons.title: Sui objects, ownership and programmable transactions
lessons.study_notes: Learn object identifiers, versions, digests, ownership and transaction dependencies. A stale object reference cannot be treated as current state. Inspect programmable transaction effects and gas handling. An EVM adapter cannot safely substitute for Sui transaction semantics.
objectives: Validate object identity and version
Inspect ownership and transaction effects
Handle gas objects and shared-object contention

lessons.title: Resolve RH before assigning a venue
lessons.study_notes: RH is an unresolved user shorthand. Robinhood brokerage, Robinhood Crypto, Robinhood Wallet and Robinhood Chain are distinct scopes. The chain has published EVM network documentation, but its existence does not establish brokerage product access or permission for this project.
objectives: Identify the exact RH platform
Separate chain capabilities from broker permissions

lessons.title: XAUUSD instrument identity and contract terms
lessons.study_notes: Treat XAUUSD as an instrument label requiring an identified venue and legal product. Obtain broker-specific units per lot, quote precision, minimum size, hours, margin, financing, stop behavior and settlement rules. COMEX futures and an OTC or CFD quote are different instruments.
objectives: Resolve spot, CFD or futures product type
Check lot units, increments, sessions and financing
Refuse unspecified broker terms

lessons.title: Gold macro context and broker risk
lessons.study_notes: Study interest-rate expectations, currency exposure, scheduled releases, session liquidity and gap risk as hypotheses to test, not fixed causal trading rules. Financing, margin and liquidation behavior depend on the selected product and broker. Test outages, wider spreads and rejected or partial fills before deployment.
objectives: Distinguish context from a validated prediction
Stress spreads, gaps and financing
Review broker exposure and settlement

lessons.title: Indicators, price action and causal feature construction
lessons.study_notes: Compute returns, moving averages, volatility and momentum from data actually available at the decision. Record window, sampling, warm-up and missing-data rules. Treat indicator patterns, support/resistance and chart interpretations as hypotheses; none is a guaranteed entry signal.
objectives: Calculate and version rolling features
Avoid incomplete-candle leakage and untracked warm-up
Separate indicators from validated forecasts

lessons.title: Supply, concentration and liquidity
lessons.study_notes: Separate supply-based valuation from executable liquidity. Inspect circulating versus total supply, issuance permissions, concentration, vesting and unlock assumptions using time-stamped sources. A familiar ticker, large market capitalization or an apparently burned authority does not establish safe exit capacity.
objectives: Separate valuation from liquidity
Inspect supply permissions and concentration
Treat unlock schedules and distribution data as sourced inputs

lessons.title: Contract permissions, fees and scam resistance
lessons.study_notes: Inspect minting, freezing, upgrade, transfer-hook, transfer-fee and allowance permissions where applicable. Read verified state as well as source. Neither an audit badge nor verified source guarantees safe behavior. Unsupported contract features require a blocked decision rather than a guessed balance or net output.
objectives: Identify relevant privileged controls
Model supported transfer deductions
Reject unsupported token or contract semantics

lessons.title: Derivatives, margin, funding and liquidation
lessons.study_notes: Distinguish spot ownership, dated futures, perpetual contracts and CFDs. Learn contract multipliers, expiry or rolling, funding or financing, mark/index prices, collateral and liquidation rules from the selected venue. Required margin is not a maximum possible loss and must not replace an independent exposure budget.
objectives: Resolve derivative specifications before modeling orders
Separate collateral from notional exposure and loss risk
Include funding, expiry, financing and liquidation scenarios

lessons.title: Oracle integrity and cross-chain dependencies
lessons.study_notes: Check oracle age, publication time, units and provenance, and reconcile conflicting providers. Bridged representations have additional custody, message and settlement dependencies. Source-chain inclusion alone does not prove destination-chain receipt or final spendability.
objectives: Reject stale or conflicting oracle inputs
Distinguish wrapped and origin assets
Track both sides of cross-chain settlement
